Starting next week, Claude's web, desktop and mobile apps run in auto mode by default on Pro, Max and Team plans: instead of asking you to approve each step, an automated check blocks risky actions, and you can switch back to manual anytime.

A new Frontier Red Team post on using Claude to formally prove large codebases free of certain bugs.

Anthropic@AnthropicAI
New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: anthropic.com/research/forma…

ChatGPT Work is rolling out to every Uber employee.

Greg Brockman@gdb
it's been great to work closely with Uber to roll out ChatGPT Work to every employee, bringing agentic capabilities to the whole company!
Praveen Neppalli@praveenTweets· Oct 22
Great to host @gdb at @Uber HQ this week. We’ve worked closely with @gdb and the @OpenAI team for several years, and it’s remarkable how much has changed.

The first piece of work we did with ChatGPT years ago was with our support team, tinkering with a 4K context window :-). That’s hard to imagine now.

Now we’re using the latest frontier models to automate engineering workflows at global scale, moving into the era of agentic engineering.

Today we’re expanding agentic capabilities across the whole company. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from @OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee. We’ve seen the shift in engineering, moving from AI helping with individual tasks to completing whole workflows, and we want to bring that same shift to teams across the business.

I’ve spoken before about the ‘AI pods’ we launched earlier this year, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to improve how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for an intense capital allocation process covering 150 cities from 15 hours to 30 minutes. That’s what I love about applied AI: combining the latest technology with the expertise of people on the ground to completely rethink what’s possible. Now we want to do that at scale.

Uber has always been a company of builders, and every day millions of people around the world rely on what we create. I can’t wait to see what the team builds.

Tracking the early site work behind data centers, including a deep dive on Sterling, a groundbreaking and site work contractor.

SemiAnalysis@SemiAnalysis_
Every data center leaves a trail before it’s built. We track all of it.

“We published a deep dive in our industrials model on a company called Sterling. They do early-stage construction: the groundbreaking, the site work. That’s the first thing that happens when one of these projects starts getting built. We were able to predict their orders were going to surge, which is exactly what happened.”

“There’s essentially this waterfall of things we can track. Electrical and cooling equipment comes after. Energy has very long lead times; everyone knows gas turbines are multiple years out. We look at all of that to ensure our timelines are accurate.”

“Pre-leasing is even earlier. Hyperscalers, neoclouds and AI labs signing lease contracts with data center operators. It helps us understand ahead of time what’s going to get built under these binding contracts that cannot be canceled.”
